record.original_question: The above definition of a bi-univalent function is difficult to under- stand. What is also meant is that the inverse function f −1 has an analytic continuation to the unit disc where it is univalent. Let σ denote the class of bi-univalent functions, namely the class of functions f (z) = z + a2 z 2 + . . . analytic and univalent in D, such that their inverses f −1 are also analytic univalent in the D. Brannan conjectures that √ a∗2 ≡ sup |a2 | = 2. σ It is known that a∗2 < 1.51 (see Lewin [517]) and that a∗2 > 43 + 0.02 (see Styer and Wright [739]). Prove or disprove the statement that, if f ∈ σ, then dn ≡ |an+1 | − |an | ≤ A for some absolute constant A with 0 < A < 1. Alternatively, what is supσ dn for n ≥ 2? (D. A. Brannan)

evidence.quote: The above definition of a bi-univalent function is difficult to under- stand. What is also meant is that the inverse function f −1 has an analytic continuation to the unit disc where it is univalent.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ denote the open unit disc. Let $S$ denote the class of functions
$$f(z) = z + a_2 z^2 + a_3 z^3 + \cdots$$
that are analytic and univalent in $\mathbb{D}$. A function $f \in S$ is called bi-univalent if its inverse $f^{-1}$ (defined on $f(\mathbb{D})$) has an analytic continuation to all of $\mathbb{D}$ which is itself univalent on $\mathbb{D}$. Let $\sigma$ denote the class of all such bi-univalent functions, and for $f \in \sigma$ write its Taylor coefficients as $a_1 = 1, a_2, a_3, \dots$.

For $n \geq 1$, define
$$d_n(f) = |a_{n+1}| - |a_n|.$$

(a) Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant $A$ with $0 < A < 1$ such that for every $f \in \sigma$ and every $n \geq 1$,
$$d_n(f) \leq A.$$

(b) For each integer $n \geq 2$, determine the value of
$$\sup_{f \in \sigma} d_n(f).$$
artifact.status_search_result: Coefficient problems for the class σ of bi-univalent functions remain notoriously open. Even the basic question of determining sup|a_2| over σ (Brannan's conjectured value √2) is still unresolved, with only bounds such as Lewin's |a_2|<1.51 and the lower bound 4/3+0.02 of Styer–Wright known. No source was located establishing the bound d_n ≤ A < 1 with an absolute constant A or computing sup_σ d_n for n ≥ 2.

status_evidence.title: On the Brannan's conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Brannan-type coefficient conjectures and notes the bi-univalent coefficient problem remains open with only partial bounds available.
status_evidence.claim: Coefficient estimates for the class of bi-univalent functions remain open, including the value of sup|a_2|.

status_evidence.title: On Brannan's coefficient conjecture and applications
status_evidence.snippet: Studies a related Brannan coefficient conjecture; the bi-univalent class σ and its higher coefficient differences are not resolved.
status_evidence.claim: No proof of an absolute bound d_n ≤ A < 1 for bi-univalent functions has been established.
